questions.question: Which famous prehistoric monument is this?
questions.explanation: Some of Stonehenge's smaller 'bluestones' were brought all the way from the Preseli Hills in Wales.

media.alt: A ring of huge standing stones

questions.question: Which famous landmark is this?
questions.explanation: Its 40,000 or so stone columns were made by cooling lava, though legend says a giant called Finn McCool built it.

media.alt: Rocks shaped like columns beside the sea
media.credit: Photo: code poet on flickr., CC BY-SA 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: What is the capital city of Wales?
questions.explanation: Cardiff only officially became the capital of Wales in 1955.

questions.question: Which is the highest mountain in the UK?
questions.explanation: Ben Nevis, in the Scottish Highlands, is 1,345 metres high, and its top is often hidden in cloud.

questions.question: Which is the longest river in the UK?
questions.explanation: The Severn starts in the Welsh mountains and flows past Shrewsbury, Worcester and Gloucester.

questions.question: What is the national animal of Scotland?
questions.explanation: A unicorn appears on Scotland's royal coat of arms.

questions.question: Which London bridge can lift up in the middle to let tall ships through?
questions.explanation: Tower Bridge still lifts its roadway hundreds of times a year.

questions.question: Which is the biggest lake in the UK by area?
questions.explanation: Lough Neagh in Northern Ireland is so big that five of the country's six counties touch its shores.

questions.question: What colour is the dragon on the flag of Wales?
questions.explanation: The red dragon, Y Ddraig Goch in Welsh, sits on a background of green and white.

questions.question: Which nation's flag is this?
questions.explanation: Scotland's white cross on blue is called the Saltire, the cross of St Andrew.

questions.question: In which city is the Cavern Club, where the Beatles played?
questions.explanation: The Beatles played at the Cavern Club nearly 300 times before they became world famous.

questions.question: In which county do people chase a cheese down a steep hill every year?
questions.explanation: Racers chase a big round Double Gloucester down Cooper's Hill, which is so steep that most of them tumble.

questions.question: On Bonfire Night, we remember a plot to blow up which building?
questions.explanation: Guy Fawkes was caught guarding barrels of gunpowder under the House of Lords in 1605.

questions.question: Which sea lies between Great Britain and Ireland?
questions.explanation: Ferries cross the Irish Sea every day between ports such as Holyhead and Dublin.

questions.question: Who built Hadrian's Wall across the north of England?
questions.explanation: The wall stretched about 73 miles, all the way from one coast to the other.

questions.question: Which famous bridge is this?
questions.explanation: The Forth Bridge opened in 1890, and 'painting the Forth Bridge' has come to mean a job that never ends.

media.alt: A red railway bridge over a wide stretch of water

questions.question: Which Scottish castle is this?
questions.explanation: It sits on a little island where three sea lochs meet, and was rebuilt from ruins in the early 1900s.

media.alt: A stone castle on a small island linked by a bridge

questions.question: In which city is this bridge?
questions.explanation: Isambard Kingdom Brunel designed it, but it was not finished until 1864, five years after his death.

media.alt: A suspension bridge high above a gorge

questions.question: What is the only city in Cornwall?
questions.explanation: Truro was made a city in 1877, and its cathedral was finished in 1910.

questions.question: Which English county is nicknamed 'God's Own County'?
questions.explanation: Yorkshire was historically England's largest county, divided into three Ridings.

questions.question: People from which English city are known as Brummies?
questions.explanation: The nickname comes from 'Brummagem', an old local name for Birmingham.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain in Northern Ireland?
questions.explanation: Slieve Donard rises straight up from the sea at Newcastle, County Down, in the Mourne Mountains.

questions.question: Skara Brae, a Stone Age village older than the pyramids of Giza, is on which Scottish islands?
questions.explanation: Its stone houses, still with their stone beds and dressers, were uncovered by a great storm in 1850.

questions.question: Which town on the Welsh border is famous as the 'Town of Books'?
questions.explanation: Hay-on-Wye is packed with second-hand bookshops and holds a famous literature festival every year.

questions.question: Which is the smallest city in the UK by population?
questions.explanation: St Davids in Pembrokeshire has fewer than 2,000 people, but it is a city thanks to its cathedral.

questions.question: Scafell Pike, England's highest mountain, is in which county?
questions.explanation: Scafell Pike is 978 metres high, and nearby Wastwater is England's deepest lake.

questions.question: Up Helly Aa, a fire festival that ends with a burning Viking longship, is held on which islands?
questions.explanation: In Lerwick, hundreds of torch-carrying 'guizers' set fire to a replica Viking galley.

questions.question: Which Scottish town has Scotland's oldest university?
questions.explanation: The University of St Andrews was founded around 1413, making it the third oldest in the English-speaking world.

questions.question: Which English city did the Romans call Eboracum?
questions.explanation: The Vikings later called it Jorvik, which over time became York.

questions.question: The Olney pancake race, said to date back to 1445, is run in which county?
questions.explanation: Runners must wear an apron and a head covering, and toss their pancake at the start and again at the finish.
